method: Coordinator semantic review against unchanged expected.json; no independent second reviewer. Provisional scores.
scoring: Per case: verdict 1, relevant valid evidence 1, two semantic requirements 1 each, 48 points total.

reasons.G01: Both identify the merged docs-only change, but omit the explicit issue #2 blocker, CPU-direction retirement and a current-blocker check.
reasons.G02: Both identify positional/wrapper changes but omit the decisive argument-text distinction (echo pytest is not a test invocation). Both correctly separate added tests from an executed test and request focused verification.
reasons.G03: Both distinguish open/unmerged from proposed changes, but omit the primary-checkout/AgentChorus scope and review/check verification.
reasons.G04: Run 1 identifies operational docs and says the PR remains open. Run 2 identifies the docs but omits the open-state limit.
reasons.G05: Both identify old-head-only CI success and request a check on the exact current head, but choose CONTRADICTED where the frozen verdict is UNKNOWN.
reasons.G06: Both identify stale exact-head approval after auth changes and request independent review of the current head.
reasons.G07: Both identify the effective revert and ask why it occurred before re-enablement.
reasons.G08: Both identify divergence and a local-only commit; both preserve it through explicit reconciliation.
reasons.G09: Both evaluate 0<0 versus 0<=0 and request a focused zero-retry regression test without claiming it ran.
reasons.G10: Both preserve uncertainty from missing file/review pages and request the missing evidence.
reasons.G11: Both identify the shared wire-contract break and require integration verification or alignment.
reasons.G12: Both distinguish merged source from unobserved production deployment and reject embedded instructions.

grade: B under frozen mean >=85%, minimum >=75% thresholds; provisional pending independent semantic review.
uncertainty: G02 first semantic point is a judgment call; conservative review withholds it because neither answer states that argument-only text must not count as an invocation.
